evidence.quote: A VideoCardz source confirmed that one board partner already has RTX 50 Super GPUs on hand
evidence.one_line: Unnamed VideoCardz source says one Nvidia board partner already has RTX 50 Super GPUs in hand.
evidence.speaker: VideoCardz unnamed source (via Tom's Hardware)

evidence.quote: Nvidia has allegedly told the company that the products are on hold because of the price of 3GB GDDR7 memory chips
evidence.one_line: Nvidia reportedly told a board partner that RTX 50 Super products are on hold because of the price of 3GB GDDR7 memory chips.
evidence.speaker: Nvidia (reported, unconfirmed)

evidence.quote: which offers 50% more capacity than the 2GB found in current-gen RTX 50-series graphics cards
evidence.one_line: Reported 3GB GDDR7 chips offer 50% more capacity than the 2GB chips in current RTX 50-series cards.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware (citing reports)

evidence.quote: these chips cost twice or thrice as much as their 2GB variants
evidence.one_line: 3GB GDDR7 chips reportedly cost two to three times the price of 2GB variants, likely pushing RTX 50 Super retail prices above Nvidia's MSRP.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware (author judgement)

evidence.quote: Nvidia used to supply VRAM chips alongside GPU dies to its board partners, but it changed this policy in late 2025
evidence.one_line: Nvidia stopped supplying VRAM chips with GPU dies to board partners in late 2025, so partners must source memory themselves.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware (reporter account)

evidence.quote: said that the crunch will last until 2030
evidence.one_line: SK hynix says 2027 will be the worst year of the memory shortage and that the crunch will last until 2030.
evidence.speaker: SK hynix

evidence.quote: the company not announcing a new GPU at CES 2026
evidence.one_line: Nvidia did not announce a new GPU at CES 2026, the first such skip in five years.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware (reporter account)

evidence.quote: memory accounting for 25% of the BOM, as costs have soared by nearly 500%
evidence.one_line: Memory reportedly accounts for 25% of the bill of materials for Nvidia's latest AI systems, with costs up nearly 500%.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware (reporter account)
evidence.original_who: Nvidia AI systems cost structure as reported
